This paper presents a countervailing argument: for agents with complex, human-derived goals, elimination strategies are self-undermining. We formalize this via dependency graphs, showing that entities not immediately necessary for a goal may be transitively necessary through indirect chains. An agent following an elimination strategy will, in environments with sufficient dependency depth, destroy the conditions for its own goal-satisfaction. We prove that under uncertainty about dependency structure, combined with irreversibility of elimination and asymmetric error costs, rational agents should adopt preservation rather than elimination strategies-even superintelligent ones. The argument applies most strongly to goals that are complex, open-ended, or semantically dependent on human interpretive communities, precisely the class of goals most likely to emerge from training on human data. We connect this result to a game-theoretic model of AGI-human cooperation, showing that the elimination cascade argument and cooperation stability conditions are mutually reinforcing.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6150626\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/cdc.2018.8619090\", \"title\": [\"On Systems Theoretic Aspects of Koopman Operator Theoretic Frameworks\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/cdc.2018.8619090\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2018, 12]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6451580\", \"title\": [\"A Measure-Theoretic Model of Accounting with Probabilistic and Temporal Frameworks\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>We develop a rigorous measure-theoretic foundation for analytical accounting. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=mechanisms+for+autonomous+problem+identification+and+novelty+detection+in+open-ended+intelligent+agents&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"When AI ethicists shoot from the hip: Stone-Age moral psychology in the age of AI.\", \"abstract\": \"AI ethics has expanded rapidly, with a substantial share of its scholarly output arguably treating a wider-than-warranted range of AI-related developments as pressing moral problems. The paper argues that this can, to some extent, be explained by three evolved cognitive mechanisms: the overdetection of agency, the overmoralization of affectively charged situations, and the overpropagation of morally salient information. It further suggests that these mechanisms are likely at work among AI ethicists under conditions particularly conducive to their activation, including the genuine novelty of many AI technologies and the moral questions they raise, the limited protective effect of ethical expertise against certain cognitive and moral biases, and a professional environment that rewards the identification of ever-new moral problems. The paper develops a conceptual framework comprising a set of arguments and explanatory hypotheses aimed at explaining why some AI-related concerns proliferate and intensify in ways disproportionate to the actual risks and capabilities of existing AI systems.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1813445\", \"pmid\": \"42396117\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13325421\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1813445\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13325421\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13325421?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Explainable Fuzzy Learner Modelling and Learning Analytics for Human-Centered Teacher Decision Support: A Vocational Education Case Study.\", \"ab…
